desc:
You are given an integer array nums and a list of queries. Each query is a pair [l, r] asking for the sum of nums[l] + nums[l+1] + ... + nums[r] (both ends included, 0-indexed).

Return an array containing the answer to every query, in the same order as the queries. Many queries can be asked about the same array, so recomputing each sum from scratch is too slow.

nums = [3, -1, 4, 1, 5], queries = [[0, 2], [1, 1], [2, 4]]
result = [6, -1, 10]
constraints: 0 ≤ l ≤ r < nums.length for every query
hints: Summing each range directly costs O(n) per query, so O(n * q) overall. Can you share work between queries?
Build an array pre where pre[i] is the sum of the first i elements, with pre[0] = 0.
editorial: Precompute prefix sums once: pre[0] = 0 and pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + nums[i]. The sum of the elements from l to r inclusive is everything up to r minus everything before l, that is pre[r + 1] - pre[l].

Building the table takes O(n) and each query is answered in O(1), so the total is O(n + q). The leading zero in pre avoids a special case when l = 0. With the given bounds every sum has absolute value at most 108, comfortably inside 32 bits.
